newsitem.title: USA: Florida lawmakers ban same sex marriages.
newsitem.headline: Florida lawmakers ban same sex marriages.

text.p: Florida's Senate came out overwhelmingly against gay marriages Tuesday, voting 33-5 in favour of a measure that would restrict the institution of marriage in the state to heterosexual couples.
Members of the state house had voted 97-19 in favour of the measure earlier in the week.

The bill now goes to Gov. Lawton Chiles who said Tuesday he had not yet decided whether he would sign or veto it. Supporters of the bill would need a two-thirds majority in each chamber to override a veto.
If Chiles signs the bill, Florida would join 18 other states that restrict legal recognition of marriages to those between opposite sexes.

Critics had said the bill marred the state's image as a tourist destination and labeled its residents as anti-gay, but its sponsor, a member of the first Republican majority in Florida's legislature since Reconstruction, said that was fine.
"I think it sends a good image," said Sen. John Grant, R-Tampa. "What we need to do is develop family tourism in Florida. What this says is that we believe in family values."
President Clinton signed the "Defense of Marriage Act," a federal law that allows states to refuse to recognise marriage between partners of the same sex, in 1996.
